subject: Onramp credits, GPU pool sizing, and bridge months for BrightLayer migration
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightlayer.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-09T16:12:00-04:00
Subject: Questions on hosted->dedicated transition economics and SLA requirements

Hi Soojin / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — BrightLayer's team is excited about moving latency-sensitive pipelines off hosted and onto a dedicated GPU pool. Before we pull procurement, I wanted to get clarity on three things so we can build the business case:

1) Conversion credits: do you provide token or dollar credits when we convert existing hosted spend into a committed Dedicated contract? If so, how are they amortized (one-time, over N months)?

2) Bridge months: we run steady spikes for month-end reporting. Would Redwood count hosted traffic toward the dedicated commit for an initial bridge period while we finish migration? If so, what limits apply?

3) Sizing + throughput guarantee: for a starting pool we're estimating 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs to meet 2k QPS peak (50-token average). What's the committed throughput guarantee you provide (p99 latency or tokens/sec) and what guardrails exist for throttling/overage?

Also, procurement will need an example term sheet and any sample SOW/attachment list (SOC2 pointers, network diagrams).

Appreciate a concise proposed structure we can present to finance.

- Samir
VP Product, BrightLayer AI
Attachments: none

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightlayer.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-09T18:40:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Questions on hosted->dedicated transition economics and SLA requirements

Samir — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then a proposed onramp we think balances economics + risk: 

Summary (TL;DR):
- Conversion credits: yes — we offer hosted-spend conversion credits up to 40% of recent 6-month trailing hosted spend, amortized as monthly offsets against the first 6 dedicated billing cycles (i.e., a 6-month taper).
- Bridge months: we can count hosted calls toward commit for up to 3 bridge months (with a soft cap at 30% of committed throughput per month) to handle cutover spikes.
- Throughput guarantees: we SLA p99 latency for configured request profiles (we commit to p99 < 350ms for the small-chat profile or 200ms for the trimmed request profile; exact numbers depend on token distribution). Dedicated pools include burst capacity options and tiered throttles — overages billed at the reserved rate or moved to hosted fallback depending on policy.

Proposed onramp structure (recommended):
1) Commitment term: 12 months reserved commit (monthly billing) for an initial pool sized at 8 A100-equivalent GPUs.
2) Credits: conversion credit equal to 30% of average monthly hosted spend over the last 6 months, applied as a dollar offset spread evenly across months 1–6. (We can increase to 40% with a 24-month commit.)
3) Bridge months: 3 bridge months where hosted API calls count up to 30% of monthly commit; additional hosted traffic billed normally.
4) SLA & guarantees: committed throughput defined as X tokens/sec per GPU (we will include measured profiling for your token distribution). SLA: p99 latency target + defined throughput floor; failure to meet floor triggers credit at a % of monthly committed fees (term sheet to specify).
5) Pricing/discounts: standard reserved discount for 12-month commit is 18% off hosted list; suggested promotional uplift: additional 6% rebate applied if BrightLayer signs within 30 days and agrees to the 3-month bridge.

I'll attach a short one-pager that shows the math for the 8-GPU pool with your numbers and an illustrative monthly amortization of conversion credits. Can we do a 30-minute call tomorrow to run the numbers with finance?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightlayer.ai>
Date: 2027-06-10T09:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Questions on hosted->dedicated transition economics and SLA requirements

Looping in a couple internal notes for the pricing model and sizing assumptions — Samir, copying so you're in the loop.

Notes:
- The 8 x A100-equivalent estimate: we'll model two sizing buckets (a) baseline 8x with avg token length 50 and 2k QPS peak; (b) conservative 12x for 10% headroom during month-end spikes. I'll attach the internal cost model (simple spreadsheet) with both scenarios.
- Conversion credit cadence: Soojin's 6-month taper is standard. If BrightLayer wants the 40% conversion credit (higher), finance will require a 24-month minimum commit. We should surface that as an option in the term sheet (40% / 24 months vs 30% / 12 months).
- Bridge behavior: implement bridge as "hosted-as-commit" with a 30% soft cap per month. Any hosted calls above that in the bridge months billed to Hosted rates. We'll gate for abuse via request profile whitelisting.

Action items (internal):
- Soojin: update the term sheet to call out the 12- vs 24-month credit options and include per-GPU throughput assumptions.
- Ben: confirm whether we can offer a one-time marketing credit (small) to help close — optional.

— Karthik
Principal, Sales Engineering
Attachments: internal_cost_model_BL_DL4521.xlsx

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightlayer.ai>

Date: 2027-06-11T10:22:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Questions on hosted->dedicated transition economics and SLA requirements

Thanks — that's very helpful. A few clarifications from procurement and infra: 

- Bridge months: BrightLayer is comfortable with a 3-month bridge but would like hosted traffic counted up to 50% of commit for the first month (to handle the cutover) then 30% for months 2–3. Is that something Redwood can accept?
- SLA: we need a documented p99 latency SLA (for our trimmed request profile) with a credit schedule (e.g., 5% monthly fee credit for not meeting p99 in >2 months out of a 12-month period).
- Conversion credits: finance prefers the 40% conversion credit but is open to 30% if we can get a 12-month commit with a 10% increase in reserved discount. Can Redwood provide a one-time onboarding credit or a trial pool for the first 30 days?

If you can update the term sheet with 1) bridge month ramp (50/30/30), 2) explicit p99 docs and credit schedule, and 3) both credit options (30%/12mo and 40%/24mo) with the revised pricing, we can circulate the package to our procurement leads.

- Samir
